feature: A new video starts from an empty timeline
summary: You can start a video from nothing: File > New Video (or Blank video on an empty window) asks for a size and a length and opens an empty timeline, V1 over Audio, with the Library ready for Import. Drag a tile onto V1 and the first clip lands there.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walk: Scripts/playtest/new-empty-video-walk.json.

try.do: Open a new empty window (Shift Command N) and click Blank video on its card, or choose File > New Video.
Press Return to take HD 1080p for 10 seconds.
Look at what opens: a black 1920 x 1080 frame, an empty V1 over an empty Audio track, the Library on Media.
Click Import Media… on the empty shelf (or File > Import Media, Shift Command I) and pick a recording.
Drag its tile onto V1 about four seconds in and let go.
Read the title bar and the end of the transport: the video grew to hold the clip.

evaluate: Is File > New Video where you would look for it, coming from Premiere's New Sequence?
Should the sheet ask for a length at all, or should a new video just be as long as what you put on it?
Does the empty Media shelf's Import Media… button feel like the obvious next step?
Is a black frame the right look for an empty video, or do you want the canvas grid showing through?
rough: The mock prints a hint under the empty tracks ('A 1920 x 1080 timeline with no clips. Import media, or open a capture from history, to begin.'). It is not built: the chrome rule allows a label of 30 characters at most there, and the empty tracks plus the Import button say it. Say if you want it.
The length you pick is a floor, not a cap: a short clip leaves black to the end of it, a long one makes the video longer. Premiere has no length at all on a new sequence.
No keyboard shortcut for New Video: Command N is New Layer, Shift Command N New Window, Option Command N New from Clipboard.
A new video that was never saved no longer reads 'saved' in its title line; it says nothing until there is a file or an edit.
